title: cybersecurity-skills coverage.json
description: An array of coverage units: one per attack surface x trust boundary x category the audit planned to review. Records what was reviewed, how, and what is still open, so 'no findings' can be told apart from 'not looked at'. validate-coverage.mjs enforces the cross-field rules (unique ids, safe paths, status-specific requirements, optional fingerprint cross-check against findings.json) and is authoritative. The coverage-ledger idea is adapted from cloudflare/security-audit-skill (MIT, Copyright (c) Cloudflare, Inc.).

surface.description: The attack surface, e.g. 'POST /api/orders/:id/refund' or 'webhook receiver'.

boundary.description: The trust boundary crossed, e.g. 'anonymous -> authenticated user', 'tenant A -> tenant B'.

owasp_category.description: OWASP category id (e.g. 'A01:2025', 'API1:2023'), or null when the unit is not OWASP-mapped.

status.description: covered: reviewed, and nothing from it was confirmed or left needs_validation; requires >= 1 reviewed path and >= 1 check, and may list only rejected fingerprints. candidate: produced at least one confirmed or needs_validation finding (or one still without a verdict); requires >= 1 finding fingerprint. blocked: requires >= 1 unresolved item.

items.description: Repo-relative path or glob. No leading slash, drive letter, ~, backslash or '..' segment.

invariant.description: The property that must hold, e.g. 'refund requires order ownership'.

method.description: How it was checked: code read, grep, test, request.

finding_fingerprints.description: Fingerprints of findings.json records raised from this unit (any verdict).

unresolved.description: Open questions or blockers left on this unit.
